edits.value_json: "The current graph 学 is arranged ⿳⺍冖子: ⺍ and 冖 form an upper assembly above 子. This visible split does not settle how traditional 學 was first constructed. One account interprets oracle-bone forms as 𦥑 (two hands) with 五 and 六, while allowing that 爻 may supply a sound cue in some forms. Separate proposals describe phonosemantic forms with 爻 as sound and 冖 as the other element; a rare, unidentified element read jù and depicted as hands or claws; and a distinct construction grouping two 臼 forms with 冖 and a following unidentified printed graphic unit to which the source assigns the sound role. That proposed role belongs to the following unit, not to either 臼 or to the whole 学 construction. The two 臼 shapes may be reduced to an abbreviated form; the exact graphic identity of that form is unresolved. The rare jù account is separate from the two-臼 proposal, though the source check notes that the graph after 冖 resembles the earlier jù-labeled graph. These are competing interpretations, not a settled reconstruction. One source also proposes learning and emulation as 學’s original meaning, but the proposal is unsettled. The modern simplified shape does not establish the ancient structure."

"The early construction accounts remain distinct. One interprets some forms as 𦥑 (two hands) with tally-like elements 五 and 六, while allowing that 爻 may supply a sound cue in some forms. Other proposals describe phonosemantic forms with 爻 as sound and 冖 as the other element; a separate, unusual element read jù and depicted as hands or claws; and a distinct construction grouping two 臼 forms with 冖 and a following unidentified printed graphic unit to which the source assigns the sound role. That role is assigned to the graph after 冖, not to either 臼 or to the whole 学 construction. The two 臼 shapes may be reduced to an abbreviated-looking graph whose identity is unresolved; the source check does not establish a human-like shape. The rare jù element is not identified as 臼. The graph after 冖 resembles the earlier jù-labeled graph, so these descriptions should not be treated as evidence that the two have different visible forms. These proposals do not establish one construction for every early form. The claim that 學’s original meaning was learning and emulation is a proposal, not an established conclusion."
